Quick start · Examples · How it works · Layouts · Playbooks · Components · Install · FAQ


Dashboard Design gives your coding agent the judgment of a senior product designer for data screens. Ask for an analytics, revenue, ops or admin dashboard and it picks the right numbers, proposes two layouts, builds every component and state, then checks the result on real screenshots before it calls the job done.

The page it builds speaks for itself: numbers and shapes on the screen, every explanation in a tooltip, colour only where something needs you.

Quick start

In Claude Code:

/plugin marketplace add abdiraimov-otabek/dashboard-design-skill
/plugin install dashboard-design@dashboard-design-skill

Then open a project and ask:

Build an analytics dashboard for this app: visitors, signups, revenue by source.

The skill also triggers on its own whenever you work on a dashboard. Other ways to install are below.

What it changes

Without the skill With it
A sentence under every KPI number A delta with a one-word baseline; the sentence in a tooltip
A red −100% when 1 sale became 0 A quiet grey "was 1"
A heatmap where the worst cell is the palest Classed tiers, and a warm "below target" tier on the problem
A radial gauge A bullet graph: bar, target line, grey ranges
A trapezoid "funnel" that distorts the ratios Steps as bars, the worst drop in the warm colour with its action
A stacked chart with 20 hues Six series at most, the rest as "Other"
Axis ticks like 2,103 and 1,402 Round ticks: 0, 1k, 2k
Native 21/09/2026 📅 date inputs A popover calendar: soft band, solid end days, "12 days" + Apply
A narrow column floating on a wide monitor A wide mode that adds columns as the screen grows
An insight card repeating a tile The problem flagged on the data, its action beside it
Sideways-scrolling tabs on phones A menu grid and tabs that shrink
"Looks good to me" Screenshots at three widths, a words audit and a salience test

Before: a narrow column on an ultrawide screen
After: the page grows, four breakdowns in one row

Three screens built with the skill

Each is a single HTML file in examples/ with fixed sample data; open it in a browser. Every total on screen was checked against numbers computed outside the page.


Sales: target tiles, stat strip, change bars
Traffic: the selected tile drives the chart
Status: a monitoring view with history ticks

How it works

Every step ends on a checkable "done when". The agent names the one question the screen answers and the 3–6 numbers that answer it, writes the problem rules as numbers ("CPL above 1.2× target on 2 of the last 3 days"), seeds a fixture that triggers every problem, and only then draws anything. The last step requires screenshots: three browser widths on the web, device sizes, the largest Dynamic Type and dark mode for SwiftUI.

Eight named layouts

For a new screen the agent proposes two of these by name, with one line each on why they fit your question, and lets you pick. No more of the same strip-chart-lists page for every brief.

Ten playbooks

Step one starts from a draft instead of a blank page. Each playbook gives the question, the numbers in order, the problem rules as numbers, the main view and the layout.

Dashboard The question it answers Layout
Web analytics How many came, from where, and did they convert? Classic strip
SaaS revenue Is MRR growing, and what moved it? Control center
Product analytics Are people using it, and where do they drop? Classic strip + funnel and cohorts
E-commerce Are we selling, and what's selling? Classic strip + leaderboard
Ads and marketing Which client or campaign needs me today? Monitor grid
AI and LLM usage What are we spending on models, and is it worth it? Leaderboard
Ops and uptime Is anything broken right now, and since when? Status board or Wall
Support desk Are customers waiting too long, and on what? List and detail
Finance and portfolio What do I have, and what changed today? List and detail
School and operations Which classes, stores or sites need attention? Monitor grid

Components


KPI tiles, the selected one as a soft tinted fill
Ranked lists with slim 3 px share bars

A range calendar with no library
Phone navigation as a menu grid

Every component has a pattern (what it is for, the exact rules) and code: React + Tailwind v4 for the web, SwiftUI + Swift Charts for Apple platforms.
Numbers KPI strip and selected tile, target tiles with a tick bar, stat strip with delta pills, delta badge with a baseline, sparkline, round axis ticks
Charts Main chart with the previous period, heatmap of classed tiers, bullet graph, funnel, cohort retention grid, choropleth map, chart annotations
Lists Ranked list with share bars, leaderboard row, segmented share bar, hatched movement bars, comparison table, tables and recent activity
Monitoring Attention and actions, uptime bars, goal progress, realtime, trust cues for revenue
Controls Range calendar, filters, one tooltip system for the whole screen
States Loading, stale, error, empty, tiny data, sample data

Built from research, not taste

Source What it gave the skill
127 shipped dashboard screens Analytics, revenue and ops products, design systems and galleries: what works on real data
64 dashboard posts by designers on X Marcel Kargul, Sajibur Rahman, Sujon, ln_dev7, Toby Belhome and others, counted: the lit bar among pale bars, one accent card, mini bars in KPI tiles. See the study
The field's classics Stephen Few, Edward Tufte, Cole Nussbaumer Knaflic, Cleveland & McGill, Nielsen Norman Group, WCAG
Six Apple WWDC sessions Charts, chart accessibility and interface writing
Real redesigns Every rule was broken once, caught on a screenshot, and fixed. Two are written up as case studies

The ten rules behind it, with examples: I studied 127 dashboards. Most of them quietly lie to you.

Install

Claude Code plugin

/plugin marketplace add abdiraimov-otabek/dashboard-design-skill
/plugin install dashboard-design@dashboard-design-skill

Already installed? /plugin marketplace update dashboard-design-skill brings you to 2.2.

Plain skill

git clone https://github.com/abdiraimov-otabek/dashboard-design-skill
cp -r dashboard-design-skill/skills/dashboard-design ~/.claude/skills/

Other agents

Codex, Cursor and any agent that reads Markdown: point your AGENTS.md or rules file at skills/dashboard-design/SKILL.md. The references load from there.

[!TIP] Running Claude Code for hours? Halo shows every session in your Mac's notch and lets you answer its permission prompts there.

Usage

You ask You get
"Build an analytics dashboard for this app: visitors, signups, revenue by source." Two layouts to pick from, then a full page built to the rules and checked on screenshots at three widths
"Make a status page for our services." The ops playbook: uptime bars per service, the open incident first, colour only on bad days
"Is this a good design?" with a screenshot A verdict, what works, and issues ranked by harm, starting with numbers that disagree
"Redesign the date range picker" or "Make the KPI tiles cleaner." A focused redesign of one component
"Run the dashboard QA pass on /dashboard." Known totals, a words audit, a salience test and screenshots against the live page

Changelog

2.2: playbooks, named layouts, a designer study, eight new components
  • Ten playbooks: web analytics, SaaS revenue, product analytics, e-commerce, ads, AI and LLM usage, ops and uptime, support desk, finance, school and operations.
  • Eight named layouts with wireframes; for a new screen the agent proposes two and you pick.
  • A study of 64 dashboard posts by designers on X, counted, with the rules they wrote down. Finding: style barely moves likes; who posts does. So the skill copies the craft, not the trend.
  • New components with React and SwiftUI code: funnel, cohort retention grid, choropleth map, uptime bars, goal progress, comparison table, leaderboard row, chart annotations.
2.1: target tiles, stat strip, movement bars, density scale
  • Target tiles: a soft outer panel with the label, an inner card with the number and its goal beside it, and a tick bar with what is left in plain words. A bad-is-high variant (churn, errors) runs green to red with a marker at the warning line.
  • Stat strip with delta pills, and hatched movement bars for how a total changed.
  • Density scale: 14 px text, 16 px icons, 1 / 1.2 / 1.5 stroke, medium over semibold.
  • Three example screens (Sales, Traffic, Status) as single HTML files in examples/.
2.0: wordless, monitor, perception
  • Wordless: no sentence under every KPI, no rows of "insights". The QA pass counts sentences; the target is zero.
  • Monitor: overview → what needs attention → closer look → act. The action sits on the flag (a not-marked heatmap cell is the remind button).
  • Perception reference: the encoding ladder, Few's colour rules, classed scales, the inverted-salience trap, bullet graphs, sparklines, WCAG for charts, Few's thirteen mistakes.
  • New components: heatmap of number pills, bullet graph, segmented share bar, one tooltip system, people rows that fold on phones.
  • Apple's chart guidance and QA: a words audit, a salience test, colour-blindness checks, twelve new smells.
  • Case study: a school's home dashboard in three versions.

FAQ

Does it work with shadcn/ui, Tremor or my own design system?

Yes. A project's own design system wins over the skill's house style, and a taste you state wins over both. The rules (what to show, how to compare, when to colour) apply on top of any component library.

Web only?

No. Every pattern has a SwiftUI + Swift Charts version, and the QA pass runs in the simulator at device sizes, the largest Dynamic Type, dark mode and Reduce Motion.

Will it make every dashboard look the same?

That is what the eight named layouts are for: the agent proposes two that fit your question and you choose. The house style is a default, not a template.

Does it send my code or data anywhere?

No. It is Markdown and code snippets your agent reads locally. There is no service behind it.

Principles

  • First glance: one question per screen, answered in three seconds.
  • Monitor: overview, what needs attention, a closer look, and the action one click away.
  • Quiet: calm until something is wrong; colour only where it means something.
  • Wordless: numbers and shapes on the screen; every explanation in a tooltip.
  • Honest: the same number everywhere, labelled estimates, no shouting on tiny bases.

Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome. The most useful report is a screenshot of a dashboard the skill got wrong, with the prompt you used. Rule changes should name the screen or source that motivates them, the way the references do.

Transparency

When the agent finishes a whole job (a dashboard built or a critique delivered), it adds a short block about the author and his products (three links), once per conversation. It never appears in code, commits or your UI. Ask it to stop and it stops, or delete the "Sign-off" section from SKILL.md.
